//system directives. not needed most of the time as the global directive file autogenerated will provide most of them. can add extra libraries there or in the specific file you need the functionality in

**using System;** <--System Directive

//namespace. used to prevent name collisions, primarily. anything within it such as variables and functions will collide if improper naming conventions are used.

  namespace HelloWorld {}


  //all executable code in a c# program needs to be wrapped within a class. The entry point of the program is located WITHIN this class, but is NOT the class itself.
  
  class Program {}

// the main entry point of the program. Must be static, and typically will not return any value, so declaring as void is common, but can also be set to an int. Not always true however, especially in CLI apps.

  static void Main(string[] args) {}
